A frustrating RNG-fest, especially on hard mode you are completely reliant on getting the correct drops at the correct times and few enough enemies spawning in a bunch. In hard mode, getting stuck on one alien is your doom - it's not fun or exciting, it's the opposite. The only required "skills" are willingness to grind tedious BS, remembering a build you hope the holy RNG-sus blesses you with and the skill of moving in procedural circles to get to the closest UI-arrow. The build would be easier to acquire if you'd not only be given 3 random skill classes, but you also have to roll for RNG to give you the specific skills from within those classes. One bad roll and your game is ruined. Such fun. Sure, the achievements "feel" like something when getting a few of the last ones is a true grind. Though anything to do with skill is thrown out the window after a certain point. Getting 50 explosions in 3 seconds could be enjoyable if I had any way to track my progress. I can't discern 30 from 40 within 3 seconds - even less 45 from 50. Finally, giving up when RNG-sus gives you the middle finger doesn't work. You have to first select your awful perk before you can nuke yourself from orbit. Gaben, plz fix.

This game has all of the right ingredients for a good game, but it stands out amongst other action-roguelikes for its lack of meaningful progress. Even when you're a handful of hours deep and have purchased a dozen performance upgrades, the experience doesn't get any easier. Every map clear feels like you barely survived and you never feel overpowered. The player has sluggish movement even with upgrades and every enemy feels like a bullet sponge. I'm hoping the game evolves towards a more fun experience as its development continues.

This game has a lot of potential, if ONLY it could stop being so dull, boring and uninspired. It is a COMPETENT game. But its not a FUN game. The art style, though overly done, is okay. Soundtrack is repetitive, but okay. Gameplay is functional and has solid foundations, but feels so boring. What sets Vampire Survivors apart from its offspring is its IMPACT. That game focuses on FEELINGS FIRST, BALANCE LATER. Its about becoming the embodiment of destruction. In Swarm Grinder, you become the embodiment of averageness. Theres no overpowered build, characters come in scarce variety (3 atm) and are slow, frail and weak. Theres no incentive to build variety since characters sinergize only with their respective skills. Upgrades, meta or not, are bland and offer flat bonuses. And weapons "evolutions" are just so lame. "Hits twice! Explodes Twice! Pierces Twice!". I feel like the structure for a GREAT game is already there, it just needs to fly. Think outside the box, dont be afraid of pushing crazy updates and go wild. This is THE game subgenre for that.

You expect games in the VS genre to be a bit grindy, hell this one even has grind in the name. But it's grindy in a way that is incredibly disrespectful of your time. An example, to level up one of the classes, you need to complete achievement type objectives. One of them is to get up to 50 attacks on a certain skill. So you take all the relevant perks related to giving you extra attacks. But those only get you up to about 30 even if you take every single one. So how do you get the achievement? You have to take this specific skill which gives you an extra attack every 4 minutes. Which means firstly, you have to roll that skill early on your first few level ups. Then you have to wait around you get enough blades, often way after you're more than able to straight out win the match just to somehow get this achievement especially if you got the upgrade late. Compound that with the fact like most games of this genre, enemies get tougher as time goes by, so chances are while you're derping around waiting to get more attacks, you'll just die because the enemies have outlevelled you because you've capped out on upgrades. To add insult to injury, some of the skills and related achievements are buggy so you could potentially waste your time grinding for 30 minutes to an hour, only to have a pleasant surprise when you realise it didn't register. And one class in particular, the Bombard, is bugged so you can't progress, AND lags so badly on certain builds it becomes a slideshow and is basically unplayable. Fantastic. And this isn't just an achievement, which might be fine if they're giving it to completionists to do. This actively blocks you levelling up the class you're playing which locks you out from using various gameplay related upgrades. I hope this review serves as a reminder to devs that Achievements aren't there for you to troll your players and waste their time. Good games are coming out every day, having BS like that to pad out playtime and waste player time is a lame strategy which should be called out every time we see it.

第一次比较认真地玩一个游戏 同时也是第一次拿到全成就 因此也是第一次在steam上做出测评。 首先先对这个游戏做出本人一个主观的评价：有一定创新的类幸存者的游戏。如果对这一游戏进行打分的话，个人认为是70-75：中等偏上的优秀小作品，但仍有不足。接下来想对以上内容做一个系统的讲述。 不可否认的，血色矿脉确实具备了其他类幸存者游戏所不具有的一些创新点(不排除因为个人玩的类幸存者游戏不多而导致的一些认知缺失 ) 1.出怪：相较于其他游戏的不同，血色矿脉出怪是取决于地图上的可视化的巢室。玩家操控的机甲具有一定的触发范围，当巢室进入触发范围内就会生成虫族(?)，因此出怪在一定程度上是可控的，但是也导致了玩家走到哪里，哪里的虫族就泛滥成灾 2.生存机制：对于机甲生存而言，一共有两个要素：生命与燃料。生命在受到攻击后会减少，燃料则是根据技能升级决定消耗数值。当生命或燃料二者有一个变为0后游戏就会失败。与生命不同，燃料每秒都会消耗。每个角色都有二层燃料过载，当获取燃料超过上限后，就会根据所选机甲获得不同的buff。而血包和燃料都会在击杀虫族后掉落，因此为了生存不得不不断击杀虫族。 3.升级机制：与其他类幸存者通过经验提升等级获得技能强化不同，血色矿脉需要在地图上找到钻机点后清理周边障碍召唤钻机进而获得三选一升级，因此击杀虫族对升级并无直接影响。 4.技能进化：技能进化不需要与其他技能搭配，只需该进行六次强化即可。每个技能拥有三种进化方向。 以上这些机制在初玩时能够给到玩家切实的新意，是值得肯定的。接下来谈谈游戏中的不足 1.本地化：翻译中存在较重的机翻痕迹，有模糊甚至错误的表述，最经典的是修复部件时“修复XXX以获得XX生化碎片”（实际是消耗碎片）。角色进阶任务和技能强化中也有模糊的表述，有时候不得不切换回英文去看才能理解含义。 2.公公又式式的进化：虽然每个技能有三种不同的进化方向，但是强度不平衡，大多数情况下只会选择某个进化。起搏器不选超越无限，屠刀不选粉碎机，加特林机枪不选三发，漩涡刃不选龙卷，后面的忘了，反正跟读四大名著不读红楼一样，品味和修养都很差😭。越打到后面选择会越公式化，加之每局2次大类重选和3次小类重选，在一定程度上促进了定式加点的趋势。 3.单调的游戏内容：虽然有3个地图6个进化(难度)，但是怪物种类也就只有六到七种（不太记得了），boss更是从头到尾都是同一朵花，攻击方式也不会随着难度有所变化，打多几遍全部怪都眼熟了。地图也是换汤不换药，洞穴=平原+障碍，花园=洞穴+毒囊。也许在解锁新进化后随之解锁的部分配件能给人带来一定探索欲，但是在相同的地图皮和怪潮下仍然会被消磨殆尽。 4.较大的角色差距：玩了这么久感觉屠夫是当之无愧的T0，外圈倍伤，超载红温，能抗能打，定位十分全面。起手就能用的机枪手在合适的构筑下(弹匣容量攻速跳弹)也能独当一面，上手难度也相对较低。当时跟着下矿的只有我(指机枪手)一个女玩家，你们(指屠夫和炸弹人)躲哪里去了？然而需要击杀50000敌人才能解锁的炸弹人就显得有点幽默了，鸡肋的超载buff(回血、加迫击炮攻速)，令人忍俊不禁的索敌机制(迫击炮、宇宙火箭)无疑是神留给机枪手和屠夫的仁慈（不排除是个人操作能力问题导致的）。 5.抽象的成就系统：虽然大多数成就都比较容易达成，但是也有彷佛特地是为了拖时间而设计的成就，例如生存35分钟和获胜25次。在完成大多数成就时本人只通关了13次，最后一个成就就是获胜25次。为了补齐剩下的12次不得不陷入屠夫平原进化0猛撞的5~6分钟速通复刷循环，快打吐了。 6.稀缺的引导：游戏中涉及到的单元格、巢室等概念并没有具体说明(或者被本人漏掉了)，虽然打多了之后能慢慢体会出来，但是有了直观的说明后能节省大量时间 当然，对于一个事物我们也要辩证地看，既要看到不好的一面，也要看到优秀的一面，既要批判，也要肯定，这样才称得上是健全。虽然上面提到了部分不足，但血色山脉也有其可取之处。 1.创新性的机制：在开头提到的创新机制无疑打破了类幸存者游戏的定式，走出了截然不同的路，能够让人眼前一亮。在游玩中能不断体会到其中的妙处。例如燃料机制与虫群机制让玩家不得不时刻处于一种战斗爽的状态以维持生存，有种为了生存而战的意味。 2.直观的局外升级：局外升级给的属性数值极高，作用到游戏中能直接体现出其效果，反馈直接。 3.技能combo：选取合理的话技能之间能形成正调节，用相互之间的属性增强相互之间的属性，起到1+1>2的效果。 大致只想到这些，也许还有本人之前想的但是在评测过程中忘掉的内容后续会追评补上。总而言之，血色矿脉应该是处于优秀线上下波动的一款类幸存者游戏，在其创新的机制下如果能够再加以完善的话能做得更好。目前的内容结合价位应该也算合适的。 当然，这些也只是个人偏主观一点的评价，如果有不同意见的话实属正常。本人主观意见不代表客观事实。一千个读者有一千个哈姆雷特，游戏体验具体如何见仁见智。 好评，推荐。

游戏基本没有什么难度，先集中点出两个能互相配合的特殊能力后，推图的压力就只剩燃料耗尽。 游戏系统的可视化和引导糟糕的差，打通难度五了子弹风暴的50+贯穿伤害都还没完成，我甚至不知道到底要怎么去完成，三种高射速武器都升满过都没完成，游戏内也没有进度条，完全不知道什么情况会推进进度。 部分词条和系统的理解也很费劲，完全没有说明，特别是那个持续时间的系统，居然是技能释放一定时间自动冷却，弹匣满的强制冷却是真的恶心。 优化也是烂得离谱，只要两个主武器升满就开始卡顿，三个主武器升满有时候怪物直接卡得不会动了，成就里居然还有使用五个主武器，真的对自己的优化没点数。 虽然价格便宜，但哪哪都不太行，完全没有可玩性，最多三四个小时就让人兴致全无。
有些特色，玩起来还不错。一些构筑成型后在高难也能痛快割草，战斗爽就完事了。 但是，麻烦优化下汉化吧，机翻我也忍了——但像屠夫VIII级任务把“和屠夫一起完成难3或以上的任意地图，不能增加‘数量’”弄成“和屠夫一起完成难3或以上花园”真是离谱了。我辛辛苦苦按照中文字面通了三次都没解锁，满怀疑惑地切到英文一看，好家伙，直教人绷不住。

前两个角色升满了，第三个角色玩得像坐牢。升级也卡轨道炮总伤害5K。 游戏就两个容易死的点，燃料没了或者被怪堆粘住硬生生磨死。 第三个角色两个全占了，不能aoe把怪秒了，捡燃料就等死吧。 特别是带上轨道炮的时候，轨道炮这玩意纯纯的five。不是做升级我都不用它，问题是这玩意速度慢也怪堆描边，带上去反而降战斗力，5K伤害的解锁也坐牢，连刷两天都打不出来。 移速只有工坊的那点蚊子腿，高难度遇上怪潮 一堆红线怪，一刻都不能停。爽不起来。 燃料设定也很屎，掉落在怪堆里面你捡不了，移速慢跑完圈回来就消失了。这玩意上限也低，存不了，哪怕生存点满也就十几秒烧完。 刷装备也很屎，一局就两个装备。还不根据已有的进行定向优化，我库里有一样或者更上级的装备，给我掉落同一装备。 出怪机制导致了高难度，就只有爆炸流这类能跟得上怪物数量成长的能扛得住。 所以第一二角色走爆炸流都是轮椅，屠夫的永恒风暴+割草机更是轮椅中的轮椅，白板装备都能全通高难。 因此，第三角色又是铁废物，清理肉怪堆只能坐牢绕圈圈。

Just launched the game for the first time in a while. All progress has been wiped and the game has been made grindier. Previously you'd launch in to a map filled with eggs, hives, mining spots and you'd have to path around and the length of the round was up to your speed and skills. Now you launch in to a blank map with 3-10 event items already spawned around you, and you are forced to run in circle for 30 minutes in the of the blandest Vampire Survivor clones I've played. I couldn't even finish a full 30 minute round, got to 25 minutes and was so bored of running in circles with nothing to break up the tedium I Alt + F4'd. This is the Temu/WISH version of Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor, which right now you can pick up for the pretty much the same price on sale. DRG:S has more maps, more weapons, more build variety, more enemies and overall just has more of everything and is better.

the game is fun, but it lacks content, there aren't enough options for upgrades to feel like there is much build variety to be had. there isn't any reason to pick more than one color of weapon on a run because theres a lot of upgrades that affect a specific class of weapon so picking all the same is just a better choice, but each type of weapon only has three weapons unless theres more to unlock so you will just have the same three every run of a specific type and thewy each only have like 6 upgrades to put into they 3 slots they have so you can just always get the three you want once you find the best combo you will have no reason to pick anything else. if the game had like twice as many upgrades and weapons to pick it would be great as the gameplay is really fun but as it is it just lacks content to make there be much reason to play past a few run in my opinion

Swarm Grinder offers a refreshing spin on the increasingly popular survivors-style roguelite genre by combining relentless combat with exploration, resource gathering, and environmental strategy. Instead of focusing entirely on surviving endless enemy waves, the game challenges players to venture across procedurally generated mining zones infested with dangerous alien organisms while searching for valuable Bioshards. Every expedition feels like a calculated risk, as pushing deeper into unexplored territory rewards players with resources and upgrades but also exposes them to increasingly aggressive alien swarms. This constant balance between exploration and survival gives the game a stronger sense of purpose than many of its genre counterparts, creating an experience that feels both familiar and surprisingly original. One of the game's defining mechanics is its evolving battlefield. Alien cells gradually spread throughout the map, transforming safe areas into dangerous territory until they are disturbed, triggering massive attacks from hostile creatures. This system ensures that players cannot remain stationary for long, encouraging continuous movement and thoughtful decision-making. Exploration becomes more than simply uncovering new terrain—it becomes a strategic necessity that directly influences the flow of each run. Since every map is procedurally generated, no two expeditions unfold exactly the same way, giving the game excellent replay value while maintaining a consistent feeling of tension from beginning to end. Combat is fast, satisfying, and built around experimentation. Weapons attack automatically, allowing players to focus on positioning, movement, and choosing upgrades that complement one another. Throughout each run, players assemble a build using a mixture of offensive and passive abilities that can evolve through branching upgrade paths. These upgrades are more than simple damage boosts, often altering the behavior and effectiveness of individual skills, encouraging players to discover powerful combinations and unique strategies. Every successful run feels partially earned through smart build planning rather than relying solely on quick reflexes, making progression rewarding for players who enjoy experimenting with different playstyles. Outside individual missions, Swarm Grinder provides a steady sense of long-term progression. Multiple playable characters each feature their own advancement systems, while gadgets, permanent unlocks, collectible items, and increasingly difficult evolution levels provide meaningful goals beyond simply surviving another run. The growing collection of skills, equipment, and upgrades steadily expands gameplay possibilities, giving players plenty of reasons to continue improving their characters and refining their preferred builds. Even after mastering the fundamentals, higher difficulty settings introduce fresh challenges that demand better planning and more efficient resource management. Visually, the game embraces colorful pixel art that successfully combines retro aesthetics with modern readability. Enemy designs are distinctive enough to remain recognizable even when dozens of creatures flood the screen, while vibrant attack effects create exciting moments without becoming overly cluttered. The science-fiction mining environments establish a convincing atmosphere where industrial machinery collides with rapidly spreading alien infestations. Combined with energetic music and satisfying sound effects, the presentation reinforces the game's frantic pace while maintaining a clear visual identity throughout extended play sessions. What truly separates Swarm Grinder from many similar roguelites is how effectively it integrates exploration into every aspect of gameplay. Rather than treating the environment as little more than a backdrop for combat, the game turns the world itself into an active participant through expanding alien growth, hidden resources, and meaningful navigation choices. Players are constantly making decisions about when to explore, when to fight, and when to retreat, creating a more strategic experience than traditional arena survival games. These mechanics help every run feel purposeful instead of becoming a repetitive exercise in defeating increasingly larger enemy waves. The game is not without its shortcomings. While the progression systems provide satisfying longevity, the overall amount of content may feel somewhat limited for players seeking hundreds of hours of variety. Veteran players may eventually become familiar with available maps and encounter patterns despite procedural generation. Additionally, the challenge curve can be demanding during the early stages, requiring patience before the deeper customization systems fully reveal their potential. Fortunately, the strong gameplay loop and rewarding experimentation help offset these limitations, making repeated attempts consistently enjoyable. Overall, Swarm Grinder succeeds by building upon the foundations of the survivors-like genre while introducing meaningful mechanics that emphasize exploration, strategic decision-making, and environmental interaction. Its combination of procedurally generated levels, flexible character progression, engaging combat customization, and dynamic alien ecosystem results in a roguelite that remains exciting well beyond its opening hours. Players looking for an action game that rewards adaptability and experimentation will find plenty to appreciate, while fans of the genre will likely enjoy its fresh ideas and polished execution. Rating: 7/10

Games like "Swarm Grinder" make me wish that Steam games could be graded on a scale instead of a thumbs up/thumbs down system. Yes, I like the game. I have 100-percented its achievements. Yes, I gave it a thumbs up, but this is a very hesitant recommendation. It does some incredibly unique things that I haven't seen yet in other action roguelikes, but it has one really, really big problem: namely, the stuttering. When everything slows down to a crawl and then FREEZES during some pretty mild firefights, I just throw my hands up and exit out of the game completely. I would have demanded a refund for any other game that froze as often as "Swarm Grinder." But it is a helluva fun game -- when it works. I kept coming back to it until I got all the Steam trophies. The solo indie dev who made this is clearly talented when it comes to game design, but for the love of God, please do something about the stuttering.
